A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Policy Contrastive Decoding study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching content across appendix relabeling.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on nine simulation and six real-world tasks, with ablations, robustness tests, CAM visualizations, and maximum-step evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains original simulation and real-world experiments, revises simulation results, and adds original latency and memory measurements in Table 5.

M1.justification: The contrastive action distribution, Track2Mask procedure, KDE-based probability estimation, and Algorithm 1 are retained. The redrawn overview and newly disclosed processing details do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine SIMPLER tasks across Google Robot and WidowX, six physical-robot tasks, and spatial, brightness, distractor, and texture variations. The increased trial counts do not expand task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain OpenVLA, Octo, and π0 with and without PCD. The annotation, detector, and inpainting alternatives also remain unchanged. The new resource analysis evaluates these existing policies.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes the reported simulation evaluation budget from 100 to 300 trials per task. Appendix E adds SIMPLER measurements of inference-step latency and memory. Task definitions, completion criteria, real-world trials, and fine-tuning settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix E assesses PCD's computational overhead across three policies, supplementing existing real-world completion times with simulation latency and memory profiling. The earlier parameter, detector, inpainting, scene-shift, CAM, and maximum-step analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1's simulation tables contain point estimates only; v3 adds 95% confidence intervals to per-task and average success rates throughout Tables 1 and 4. Together with the reported increase from 100 to 300 trials, this substantially expands statistical reporting, although interval construction remains unspecified.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 4 replace most simulation estimates under the increased trial budget. Table 1's maximum relative improvements for OpenVLA, Octo, and π0 change from 41%, 31%, and 8% to 50.6%, 29.7%, and 8.9%. Table 5 adds resource measurements. These revised estimates use different sample counts; Figures 3–5 retain their underlying outcomes.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, the action-dimension independence assumption, and Equations (1)–(3) are retained. The notation correction following Equation (2) does not change the mathematics. Neither version adds formal proofs.

C1.justification: Headline empirical magnitudes are revised: the abstract's π0 simulation improvement changes from 8% to 8.9%, and the introduction updates the OpenVLA and Octo improvements. The central claims of training-free, plug-and-play mitigation across autoregressive and diffusion-based policies remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly explains latency through the second forward pass, memory differences through serial versus parallel processing, and the smaller end-to-end delay through physical robot execution time. The earlier generalization interpretations and stated limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly documents serial processing of original and masked inputs for OpenVLA and parallel processing for Octo and π0. Existing fine-tuning hyperparameters, KDE sample count, model-source links, and project link are retained. These are additional disclosures without an established implementation change.

R1.justification: v3 removes citations and references to ManiWav, CoT-VLA, and FALIP. This is limited citation pruning; the positioning relative to robotic foundation models and visual contrastive decoding remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained, with localized edits to the introduction, contributions, and Section 4.4. Citations switch to author-year style, Appendix A.1–A.4 becomes A–D, and new appendices cover computational overhead and LLM writing assistance.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn and relocated, while Figure 5 changes from deviation plots to labeled grouped bars. Figures 3–4 adopt percentage axes, Tables 1 and 4 are reformatted for confidence intervals, Table 5 is added, and title, header, and appendix layouts change.

improvement.justification: The expanded simulation evaluation, confidence intervals in Tables 1 and 4, and resource profiling in Table 5 improve empirical transparency. Redrawn Figures 2 and 5 also clarify the presentation. The gain is limited by unspecified interval construction and a new Appendix E error attributing Figure 3's π0 timing result to OpenVLA.
